pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches

schema.name: ToolSearch
schema.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

1	# Swarm guide
2	
3	One process, one asyncio loop, many agents. Agents share a **blackboard**; the **orchestrator** runs them in phases.
4	Each person owns **one file in `agents/`** (no merge conflicts); shared code is in `swarm/` (change it by PR, small).
5	
6	```
7	COLLECT (dataflow: scrapers + analysts, synchronised by done flags)  ->  VERIFY  ->  COMPUTE (plain code)  ->  SUBMIT
8	 scrapers save pages the MODEL chose; analysts turn them into results                                        enter bid, sign TAN
9	```
10	
11	## Data flow (who waits for what)
12	
13	```
14	BriefReader ──> results["brief"] (reference, scenario date, bidder, authorised senders), results["sites"] (role -> siteId)
15	TenderScraper (b0) login + overview, then documents (main tab) || Q&A (2nd tab)
16	                   ──tender.page──> done.tender ──> QuantityAnalyzer ──> results["tender"], results["quantities"]
17	SpecScraper   (b1) ──spec.page───> done.spec ───> RequirementAnalyzer ──> results["spec"], results["requirements"]
18	                                                        (+ Q&A amendments) ──> results["requirements_final"]
19	ErpScraper    (b2) logs in while waiting for results["requirements"]; then small jobs on up to ERP_TABS tabs: one
20	                   search per catalogue group -> the listed materials that fit -> record -> prices || stock per active material
21	                   ──erp.page──> done.erp ──> MaterialMatcher ──> results["erp"], results["materials"]
22	MailScraper   (b3) logs in while the brief is read; one search for the reference, reads every message about the tender
23	                   ──> done.mail_core; then a search per brief topic still without a valid message (parallel tabs)
24	                   ──> done.mail ──mail.page──> DiscountAnalyzer ──> results["discount"], results["mail"], results["mailbox"]
25	CollectionCoordinator (reasoning model) as each site's first pass + analysis is done: code lists the gaps (facts the
26	                   bid needs that no saved page holds), the model turns them into focused follow-up jobs on that site,
27	                   the affected analyses run again ──> results["gaps"] (what is still open when COLLECT ends)
28	PopupGuard (next to every browse): clears cookie banners, surveys, notices, error pages, access gates
29	EvidenceVerifier ──> results["verification"];  BidCalculator ──> results["bid"], results["answer"]
30	BidSubmitter (b0 main tab, full reasoning; TAN via a short browse on b3's main tab) ──> results["submission"]
31	```
32	
33	Every scraper sets its `done.<role>` flag in a `finally`, so analysts never wait forever; every wait has a timeout
34	bounded by `ctx.time_left()`. Missing inputs degrade the bid (omitted positions, blank breakdown fields), never crash it.
35	
36	## Files
37	
38	| Path | What |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| `swarm/blackboard.py` | `Evidence(kind, site, data, source, author, note)`, `Blackboard` (post/query/set/get/wait_for/dump/load) |
41	| `swarm/agent.py` | `Agent` base, `Phase`, `@register` |
42	| `swarm/context.py` | `ctx`: `task`, `board`, `llm`, `pool`, `site(id)`, `brief`, `time_left()`, `seconds_left()`, `lock(name)`, `shared` |
43	| `swarm/llm.py` | `ctx.llm.chat / ask / ask_json` (Qwen, concurrency-limited, usage counted), `parse_json` |
44	| `swarm/browser_agent.py` | `browse(ctx, goal, browser=n, tab=..., flash=..., careful=...)`: **browser-use** on our CDP browser + Qwen, with our actions `read_page`, `record`, `fill_form`, `share_tip`, `read_document`, `read_visual`; `Tab` |
45	| `swarm/guard.py` | `PopupGuard`: runs next to every browsing agent and clears noise (model decides once per kind of popup, cached per site) |
46	| `swarm/page_text.py` | the page extractor behind `read_page` (iframes, collapsed sections, tooltips, canvas labels, zero-width chars) |

Each person owns **one file in `agents/`** (no merge conflicts); shared code is in `swarm/` (change it by PR, small).

```
COLLECT (dataflow: scrapers + analysts, synchronised by done flags)  ->  VERIFY  ->  COMPUTE (plain code)  ->  SUBMIT

```

## Data flow (who waits for what)

```

TenderScraper (b0) login + overview, then documents (main tab) || Q&A (2nd tab)
                   ──tender.page──> done.tender ──> QuantityAnalyzer ──> results["tender"], results["quantities"]
SpecScraper   (b1) ──spec.page───> done.spec ───> RequirementAnalyzer ──> results["spec"], results["requirements"]
                                                        (+ Q&A amendments) ──> results["requirements_final"]
ErpScraper    (b2) logs in while waiting for results["requirements"]; then small jobs on up to ERP_TABS tabs: one
                   search per catalogue group -> the listed materials that fit -> record -> prices || stock per active material
                   ──erp.page──> done.erp ──> MaterialMatcher ──> results["erp"], results["materials"]

                   ──> done.mail ──mail.page──> DiscountAnalyzer ──> results["discount"], results["mail"], results["mailbox"]
CollectionCoordinator (reasoning model) as each site's first pass + analysis is done: code lists the gaps (facts the
                   bid needs that no saved page holds), the model turns them into focused follow-up jobs on that site,
                   the affected analyses run again ──> results["gaps"] (what is still open when COLLECT ends)
PopupGuard (next to every browse): clears cookie banners, surveys, notices, error pages, access gates
EvidenceVerifier ──> results["verification"];  BidCalculator ──> results["bid"], results["answer"]
BidSubmitter (b0 main tab, full reasoning; TAN via a short browse on b3's main tab) ──> results["submission"]

2	
3	This is the persistent problems list from the fresh review. A passing helper test is not proof that an unfamiliar site's complete workflow will succeed. Runtime navigation remains the model's responsibility; no production routes, answers, or scenario data belong in the package.
4	
5	| Problem | Current treatment and remaining work |
6	| --- | --- |
7	| 1. Finished browser history mistaken for accepted submission | Browser success checks the success flag. The submitter retries until it records an exact receipt quote on the tender portal. The orchestrator fails explicitly without a receipt. Receipt semantics still depend on the model interpreting the page correctly. |
8	| 2. Wizard advances after failed fills | Hidden controls are excluded; unknown radio values fail; contenteditable and shadow controls are supported. Failed or unverified fields block the helper's continue click. Values are rechecked after rendering; ambiguous visible matches require model intervention. Complex custom widgets still need further coverage. |
9	| 3. Deadline and cancellation leaks | Per-run monotonic clock, 55-second model attempts, shared concurrency limit, bounded browsing, coordinator child cleanup, and TAN cleanup. Keep measuring actual hosted-model latency and remaining signing time. |
10	| 4. Unverified material selected as exact | Final selection requires active status and every required attribute verified. Broader candidates remain available for exploration. |
11	| 5. Old specification rows or reserves reused | Only the identified current revision supplies requirements; technical releases must match that revision. Missing revision evidence must trigger collection rather than guessed fallback. |
12	| 6. Commercial authority and validity gaps | Missing sender/domain/date authority rejects messages; FX uses its condition key; date-only validity includes the full day; replacement index messages do not resurrect old windows. Named IANA time zones and UTC offsets are respected; malformed replacement discount approvals cannot revive older approvals. Broader typed commercial-entry validation remains. |
13	| 7. Missing costs silently treated as zero | Unresolved costs are explicitly marked as estimates; quantity and schema/arithmetic validation added. Best-effort partial pricing remains: estimates are not a claim of complete commercial correctness. Unpriced members retain their setup-pool shares; incomplete bonus membership and unresolved conditional discounts are marked unknown. Invalid optional fields are removed independently; malformed required lines are omitted and totals recomputed. |
14	| 8. Coordinator exhausts gaps before dispatch | Only scheduled/skipped gaps count as tried; failed jobs can retry; child jobs are cancelled and awaited at cutoff. Unscheduled jobs remain eligible. |
15	| 9. Stale page cache and failed extraction cache | Reads are live by default; full URLs retain fragments; extraction failures can retry. Completed mail/ERP extractions survive sibling cancellation. |
16	| 10. ERP starts late and discards candidates | Every newly saved spec page triggers analysis. ERP continuously queues new requirements, no first-three candidate cap, record before prices/stock, stock keyed by plant and location. Overall model/time limits still bound coverage. |
17	| 11. Guard cache/action mismatch | Button order is part of the signature and same-origin error retry navigation is permitted. Guard classification is nonblocking. Dynamic gate decisions require unchanged observed text; retry counts are scoped to the current URL. Concurrent page mutations remain a risk. |
18	| 12. Non-HTML evidence unavailable | Open shadow-root extraction, PDF/text/ZIP document tool, and explicit screenshot transcription fallback added. Cross-origin frames, image-only multipage documents, closed shadow roots, and large documents require broader evaluation. |
19	| 13. Local/sandbox browser lifecycle differs | Local runs create persistent CDP browsers, matching sandbox tab reuse. Browser calls share usage accounting. Browser-use pinned because private integration hooks remain a maintenance risk. |
20	| 14. Unfamiliar site orientation | Incomplete mappings retry; the model can request inspection of opaque sites. Multiple roles may share a site. A runtime capability-report tool invalidates contradicted mappings and triggers scraper remapping. |
21	| 15. Recorded facts missed by downstream analysis | Direct records retain observed page text; fact-role overrides route evidence to the relevant analyst. Typed extraction/provenance validation is still incomplete. |
22	| 16. SPA state and pagination | URL fragments preserved, live reads default, shadow pagination controls supported, changes polled and repeated pages stopped. Infinite-scroll/virtualized lists and slow updates need dedicated cases. |
23	| 17. Form variants | Browser regressions cover hidden duplicates, invalid radios, editable elements, and open shadow roots. Add asynchronous rerender and accessible composite-widget cases. |
24	| 18. Public UI habits treated as universal | Hints are explicitly tentative and general browser instructions require observing the UI. Several role-specific prompts still describe likely workflows; reduce these assumptions with broader fixtures. |
25	| 19. Information moves between applications | Role overrides support facts discovered on a different site; role mapping permits shared workspaces. Fully capability-based scheduling across arbitrary site counts remains future work. |
26	| 20. No held-out workflow benchmark | Browser helper tests and an opt-in live-model plain/shadow navigation evaluation added. Full workflow proof requires sandbox acceptance; an unseen multistep signing/ERP/mail benchmark is still needed. |
27	
28	Run deterministic checks with `uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q`.
29	With the local model proxy running, `uv run --no-sync python scripts/evaluate_navigation.py` evaluates randomized synthetic routes and identifiers in plain HTML and shadow DOM. It reports evidence capture separately from model completion, with steps, time, and calls. It does not use the public challenge's answers.
30	
31	Sandbox run notes and logs stay under ignored `.swarm/runs/`; they must not be copied into this document or shipped.
32	
33	The second implementation batch also streams tender and specification extractions independently, reapplies late Q&A to original revision facts, reserves eight minutes for submission, and bounds connection establishment separately from generation time. Full-workflow acceptance must still be checked in a fresh sandbox run.
34	
35	Signing investigation found a read-only amount caption mistaken for a checkbox, alongside a discount rendered with a decimal point where the wizard required a decimal comma. The submitter now formats both monetary values and discount consistently, and the form helper identifies read-only outputs. Duplicate mailbox unlock gates are filled within the exact model-selected gate; the helper does not guess between identical labels. Repeated browser-state timeouts now end the browsing connection after two bounded attempts, allowing the caller to reattach to the existing tab. These fixes require a fresh full-workflow sandbox evaluation.
36	
37	The collection follow-up saves each paginated page before advancing and reports the number of pages read, so interruptions retain evidence and the model does not mistake the final visible page for the only page collected. Incomplete traversals cannot satisfy cached reads. Tender overview collection has a short budget and no longer requires opening the submission wizard. Mail instructions prioritize actual messages on each index page. ERP jobs extract their own evidence under per-page locks, publish completed results immediately, and preserve records across retries. A slow unrelated extraction cannot hold every search behind it. The coordinator treats saved-but-unextracted Q&A as a gap; skipping an optional gap requires a matching source quote, while missing positions and specification requirements cannot be skipped. The quote check verifies provenance; interpreting whether it proves absence remains a model decision.
38	
39	`uv run --no-sync python scripts/evaluate_signing.py` runs the actual submitter and hosted model against generated local portal/mail pages. It requires decimal-comma inputs, reading a TAN behind duplicate gates, accepting a native confirmation dialog, and recording the resulting receipt. It reports server acceptance separately from receipt recording. This is a signing regression, not a full collection or pricing evaluation. TAN recording now ends the mailbox lookup directly; unlocked inline gates cannot cause the guard to classify the entire mailbox as a new gate. Looking up a known site role no longer waits for unrelated role discovery.
40	
41	Native-dialog callbacks must return immediately: cdp-use awaits asynchronous callbacks inside its sole WebSocket receiver, so awaiting a CDP response there blocks its own receiver. Dialog dismissal now runs in a tracked background task, including newly created tabs; tasks are cleaned up with the browsing session. Repeated notifications for an open dialog share one dismissal until its close event, while a later dialog remains eligible. The regression exercises the real event registry and watchdog registration contract.

Mail instructions prioritize actual messages on each index page. ERP jobs extract their own evidence under per-page locks, publish completed results immediately, and preserve records across retries. A slow unrelated extraction cannot hold every search behind it. The coordinator treats saved-but-unextracted Q&A as a gap; skipping an optional gap requires a matching source quote, while missing positions and specification requirements cannot be skipped. The quote check verifies provenance; interpreting whether it proves absence remains a model decision.

`uv run --no-sync python scripts/evaluate_signing.py` runs the actual submitter and hosted model against generated local portal/mail pages. It requires decimal-comma inputs, reading a TAN behind duplicate gates, accepting a native confirmation dialog, and recording the resulting receipt. It reports server acceptance separately from receipt recording. This is a signing regression, not a full collection or pricing evaluation. TAN recording now ends the mailbox lookup directly; unlocked inline gates cannot cause the guard to classify the entire mailbox as a new gate. Looking up a known site role no longer waits for unrelated role discovery.

Native-dialog callbacks must return immediately: cdp-use awaits asynchronous callbacks inside its sole WebSocket receiver, so awaiting a CDP response there blocks its own receiver. Dialog dismissal now runs in a tracked background task, including newly created tabs; tasks are cleaned up with the browsing session. Repeated notifications for an open dialog share one dismissal until its close event, while a later dialog remains eligible. The regression exercises the real event registry and watchdog registration contract.

3	Reviewed checkout: e5b58fc (initially detached and clean). Read current orchestration, scrapers, analysts, evidence extraction, forms, pricing, submission and tests. 6

8	
9	- Platform status: rehearsal, submitted, eligible, quality 36.9/100, 305 calls, duration 2,011,315 ms (33 minutes 31 seconds).
10	- Exactly two of five positions were submitted. The other three have no scored position fields.
11	- Both submitted positions received material, quantity, base-price and packaging credit. Neither received final-unit-price or delivery credit. Surcharge values were absent. One position received rebate credit; the other had no rebate answer.
12	- Decision, reference, discount and withdrawn-answer checks received credit. The total, total-consistency and index-window checks received zero.
13	- At elapsed 23:13.8, the last visible ERP browse ended after 30 steps with 19 records. This establishes a long job ending; it does not prove the job was successful or every earlier ERP group was explored.
14	- At 23:45.1 the matcher reported three positions with no exact match among the ERP records read. Verification logged these missing materials, calculation omitted them, and submission started immediately with about 96 minutes of platform time still available. No repair phase intervened.
15	- The wizard reached signing at about 30:43. Acceptance followed near the end of the 33:31 run. Submission consumed roughly 9 minutes 46 seconds from handoff to acceptance.
16	- The submission trace includes a certification-option mismatch and two AgentOutput validation failures. Native confirmation handling repeated approximately once per second, but the platform nevertheless accepted the answer. This trace alone does not prove a CDP receiver deadlock occurred in this run.
17	- The run used a two-hour rehearsal clock: elapsed 23:45 plus logged 5,775 seconds remaining totals approximately 7,200 seconds. A local cached challenge document also distinguishes two-hour rehearsals from 20-minute scored runs.
18	
19	The arithmetic consistency score should not be diagnosed as a summation bug from this evidence alone: the logged total equals the sum of the two logged quantity-times-unit-price values. The criterion may depend on completeness or platform semantics. Inspect the actual criterion before changing the arithmetic.
20	
21	## Limits of historical attribution
22	
23	The CLI and filtered MCP log queries returned the end of collection and submission, but no detailed earlier analyst/collection trace. The precise reason each of the three material searches failed cannot be established from these retained lines: missing source pages, incomplete requirements, stale revisions, missing reserves and extraction errors remain distinguishable hypotheses.
24	
25	Package metadata, model-call profile and timing-profile requests failed or timed out. Therefore byte-for-byte identity of the uploaded package with the checkout was not established, nor were model latency/queueing statistics recovered. The current code and observed matching/calculation output are consistent; this is not proof of package identity. The 305-call figure comes from platform status, not the incomplete local usage counter.
26	
27	## Confirmed code problems
28	
29	1. Deadline phase loss: orchestrator.py applies the collection deadline to VERIFY and COMPUTE. When collection reaches that cutoff, both can be skipped; the submitter defaults to an empty bid. SWARM_DEADLINE_S only applies locally without a finite platform clock and when scored=False, so it cannot enforce a scored-length sandbox rehearsal. A sandbox token sets scored=True for a rehearsal too.
30	2. Nominal dataflow still contains barriers: quantities wait for done.tender, material extraction waits for done.erp, and mail extraction starts only at done.mail_core/done.mail. Early spec publication uses topic keywords and can race cancellation. Material matching runs once and can use provisional mail without revisiting later evidence.
31	3. Stale ERP queue: _queue initializes only once from the first requirements result. Later requirements/amendments do not update it. Each group browse decrements pending in finally even after errors, and done.erp can be published on cutoff while work remains. Jobs represent attempts rather than demonstrated coverage.
32	4. Evidence loss: read_one emits a paginated bundle only after traversing it; interruption loses prior pages from that action. Stored text is capped at 120,000 characters without a completeness marker. Non-list extraction truncates to 160,000 characters. Failed mail extractions are cached as empty dictionaries. Analysts mostly ignore direct records.
33	5. Unverified matches: requirements filtering uses current-revision rows or falls back to all rows. requirements.setdefault retains the first row for a reference. A reserve found by explicit key is not checked against current revision. Unknown material status can be selected, and multiple active matches resolve to the first candidate. Stock locations are keyed without including plant.
34	6. Weak commercial validation: missing sender/domain/date information can relax acceptance instead of preserving uncertainty. FX selection ignores the extracted condition FX key. Index summarization can keep an older applicable rate after a newer replacement message has no applicable window. Date parsing treats non-ISO named-zone dates as UTC.
35	7. Missing values become prices: missing surcharge, packaging, pool or bonus amounts are effectively zero in final calculation; unknown conditional discount scope defaults to base_only. Shared setup, bonus, threshold and demand calculations use priced positions, which can give wrong values for otherwise known positions when another member is unpriced. These missing costs are not comprehensively reported by verification.
36	8. No recovery loop: EvidenceVerifier logs issues and cannot request another search or extraction. Source-topic labels and model done flags stand in for actual coverage. Missing material leads straight to omission while substantial rehearsal time remains.
37	9. Browser success and form safety: history.is_done() is treated as successful completion. fill_fields still performs then_click after failed fields, radio lookup falls back to the first control, visibility checks miss CSS-hidden duplicates, and assignments are not verified after asynchronous rerenders. Every browse makes a new session and its URL-bearing task can trigger an initial root navigation.
38	10. Signing observability: BidSubmitter records model done/summary, not independently verified acceptance. agent.py prints that the bid was entered and signed whenever site submission returns None. Long nested TAN lookup and per-step/model timeout settings can consume most of a scored budget.
39	11. Accounting misses browser calls: ctx.llm's semaphore/counters do not cover browser-use's separate model client.
40	
41	## Corrections to the supplied implementation summary
42	
43	- e5b58fc already includes all four-site parallelism and up to three ERP workers; introducing a swarm again is not the next improvement.
44	- The older unimplemented slider hook is absent. The current fill_form can set range values and checkboxes and dispatch input/change, guided by the model. It still needs observed bounds, correct gate scope and postcondition checks.
45	- Current canvas extraction reads aria-label or fallback text, not actual pixels. The older explicit canvas screenshot helper was removed with sites.py. Blanket claims that read_page can read all locked mail are also unsafe.
46	- Decimal is a keeper. The task's currency rule requires cent-rounding the converted base before downstream calculations, and cent allocations have their own prescribed rounding. Final component rounding must be audited against those rules; 'one rounding everywhere' would be a regression.
47	- Later work contains useful isolated fixes, but its tree adds roughly 4,100 lines and removes roughly 650 across 41 files. Port selected behaviors with narrow tests rather than importing the entire coordinator/guard rewrite.
48	
49	## Verification performed
50	
51	The existing suite passed: 42 tests, using .venv/Scripts/python.exe. This local environment uses Python 3.14, not the documented 3.12 sandbox runtime. Tests validate mostly helper behavior and faked orchestration; they do not establish end-to-end coverage, 20-minute completion, or reliable live signing. No new score or performance claim is made.
52	
53	The staged implementation prompts are in docs/IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md. Run-specific values remain outside tracked deliverables.

"""Runs the registered agents phase by phase. Agents of one phase run concurrently; a failing agent never stops others.

Time: COLLECT/ANALYZE are cut off when the useful time is gone (ctx.time_left() <= 0); VERIFY and COMPUTE (plain code,
instant) and SUBMIT always run.
Local dev: SWARM_ONLY=a,b runs only those agents; SWARM_BOARD_IN=.swarm/board.json preloads a saved board (ignored
in scored runs). The board is dumped to .swarm/board.json after every phase.
"""
import asyncio
import importlib
import logging
import os
import pkgutil
from pathlib import Path

import agents as agents_pkg
from swarm.agent import REGISTRY, Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.browser_pool import BrowserPool
from swarm.context import FINAL_MARGIN_S, Context
from swarm.llm import LLM

log = logging.getLogger("swarm")
BOARD_DUMP = Path(".swarm/board.json")


def discover() -> list[type[Agent]]:
    """Import every module in agents/ so its @register decorators run."""
    for mod in pkgutil.iter_modules(agents_pkg.__path__):
        importlib.import_module(f"agents.{mod.name}")
    return list(REGISTRY)


def select(classes: list[type[Agent]], only: str | None) -> list[type[Agent]]:
    if not only:
        return classes
    wanted = {n.strip() for n in only.split(",") if n.strip()}
    return [c for c in classes if (c.name or c.__name__) in wanted or c.__name__ in wanted]


# Plain-code phases (cross-checks, the bid arithmetic) take well under a second: they run even when collecting used up
# its time, otherwise the submitter would get no bid at all (it then omits every position).
ALWAYS = (Phase.VERIFY, Phase.COMPUTE, Phase.SUBMIT)
QUICK_BUDGET_S = 30


async def _run_agent(agent: Agent, deadline_bound: bool) -> None:
    try:
        budget = agent.ctx.time_left() if deadline_bound else agent.ctx.seconds_left() - FINAL_MARGIN_S
        if agent.phase in (Phase.VERIFY, Phase.COMPUTE):
            budget = max(budget, QUICK_BUDGET_S)
        await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(), timeout=max(1.0, budget))
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, "timed out")
        log.warning("%s timed out", agent.name)
    except Exception as error:
        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
        log.exception("%s failed", agent.name)


def _position_keys(tender: dict) -> dict:
    try:
        from agents.compute_bid import position_keys
        return {str(p.get("position")): position_keys(tender.get("clarifications") or [], str(p.get("position")))["keys"]
                for p in tender.get("positions") or []}
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - a summary must never fail a run
        return {"error": str(error)[:80]}


def board_summary(board: Blackboard) -> dict:
    """A compact view of what the swarm knows (one log line), so a run's log shows it even if early lines are lost."""
    r = board.results
    erp = r.get("erp") or {}
    return {"pages": {k: sum(1 for e in board.evidence if e.kind == f"{k}.page") for k in ("tender", "spec", "erp", "mail")},
            "positions": len((r.get("tender") or {}).get("positions") or []),
            "qa": len((r.get("tender") or {}).get("clarifications") or []),
            "requirements": sorted(r.get("requirements") or {}),
            "materials": {p: (m.get("material"), m.get("reason")) for p, m in (r.get("materials") or {}).items()},
            "erp": {"materials": len(erp.get("materials") or {}), "conditions": len(erp.get("conditions") or []),
                    "stock": sorted(erp.get("stock") or {})},
            "discount": r.get("discount"),
            # which release mails were resolved, and which keys the Q&A gave each position: the two sides that must
            # meet for packaging, commitments, setup pools, project bonus and condition groups
            "mail_topics": {t: sorted(v) if isinstance(v, dict) else v for t, v in (r.get("mail") or {}).items()},
            "position_keys": _position_keys(r.get("tender") or {}),
            "open_gaps": [g.get("id") for g in r.get("gaps") or []],
            "tips": sum(len(v) for v in (r.get("tips") or {}).values()), "errors": len(board.errors)}


async def run_swarm(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool, env=os.environ):
    board = Blackboard()
    preload = env.get("SWARM_BOARD_IN")
    if preload and not scored:                       # never replay data in a scored run
        board = Blackboard.load(Path(preload))
    ctx = Context(task=task, board=board, llm=LLM(), pool=BrowserPool(playwright), scored=scored)
    classes = select(discover(), None if scored else env.get("SWARM_ONLY"))
    from swarm.browser_agent import _MAIN_TABS, _OWNERS, _OPENERS
    from swarm import guard
    _MAIN_TABS.clear()
    _OWNERS.clear()
    _OPENERS.clear()
    guard._DECISIONS.clear()
    guard._PENDING.clear()
    log.info("agents: %s", [c.__name__ for c in classes])
    try:
        await ctx.pool.prepare()
        for phase in Phase:
            agents = [c(ctx) for c in classes if c.phase == phase]
            if not agents:
                continue
            bound = phase != Phase.SUBMIT
            if phase not in ALWAYS and ctx.time_left() <= 0:
                log.warning("skipping phase %s: out of time", phase.name)
                continue
            log.info("phase %s: %s (%.0fs left)", phase.name, [a.name for a in agents], ctx.seconds_left())
            await asyncio.gather(*(_run_agent(a, bound) for a in agents))
            if phase == Phase.COLLECT:
                # Guard classification tasks are collection work too. None may survive into signing.
                pending = list(guard._TASKS)
                for t in pending:
                    t.cancel()
                await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
                from agents import analyze_discount, analyze_materials, analyze_quantities, analyze_requirements
                await analyze_quantities.publish(ctx)
                await analyze_requirements.publish(ctx)
                await analyze_discount.publish(ctx)
                await analyze_materials.publish(ctx)
                log.info("board after collect (%.0fs left): %s", ctx.seconds_left(), board_summary(board))
            if not scored:
                board.dump(BOARD_DUMP)
        log.info("model calls: %d tokens: %s errors: %d", ctx.llm.calls, ctx.llm.tokens, len(board.errors))
        if (task.get("submission") or {}).get("kind", "api") != "api":
            receipt = board.get("submission") or {}
            if not receipt.get("accepted"):
                raise RuntimeError("No confirmed portal receipt; the run did not verify submission")
            log.info("portal acceptance confirmed: %s", receipt.get("reference"))
            return None                      # a "site" submission was entered by the submitter agent
        answer = board.get("answer")
        if answer is None:
            raise RuntimeError("No schema-valid API answer was produced")
        return answer
    finally:
        pending = list(guard._TASKS)
        for t in pending:
            t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
        await ctx.pool.close()
        if ctx.llm._client is not None:
            await ctx.llm._client.close()

"""Everything an agent gets: the task, the blackboard, the model, the browsers and the clock."""
import asyncio
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import run as contract
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.llm import LLM

# Collecting and analysing stop this long before expiry; the rest belongs to SUBMIT (filling the bid form and signing
# takes several minutes of browser steps). SUBMIT itself stops FINAL_MARGIN_S before expiry.
# signing 4 positions took 466 s in run_7732ba545b50b3a5 and ended 60 s before expiry; a 5th position adds ~90 s
SUBMIT_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 600))
FINAL_MARGIN_S = 40
# A scored run lasts 20 minutes; test runs may last 2 hours. Every run plans with at most RUN_LIMIT_S from process
# start, so test runs show the timing (and the follow-ups that fit) of a scored run. The run's real expiry still wins
# when it is earlier.
RUN_LIMIT_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_RUN_LIMIT_S", 1200))


@dataclass
class Context:
    task: dict
    board: Blackboard
    llm: LLM
    pool: object                      # swarm.browser_pool.BrowserPool (None in unit tests)
    scored: bool = False              # True in a real run (has a run token); False for local scouting
    t0: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    monotonic_start: float = field(default_factory=time.monotonic)
    _locks: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)
    shared: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)   # in-memory objects agents share (queues); never dumped

    @property
    def brief(self) -> str:
        return self.task["brief"]

    def site(self, site_id: str) -> dict:
        """The access entry (siteId, url, credentials) of a website, e.g. ctx.site("erp")."""
        for entry in self.task["access"]:
            if entry.get("siteId") == site_id:
                return entry
        raise KeyError(f"no site {site_id!r}; have {[s.get('siteId') for s in self.task['access']]}")

    @property
    def site_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        return [s.get("siteId") for s in self.task["access"]]

    def seconds_left(self) -> float:
        left = contract.seconds_left(self.task)
        simulated = os.environ.get("SWARM_DEADLINE_S")          # local runs: pretend the run lasts this long
        if left == float("inf") and simulated and not self.scored:
            return float(simulated) - self.elapsed()
        return min(left, RUN_LIMIT_S - self.elapsed()) if RUN_LIMIT_S > 0 else left

    def time_left(self) -> float:
        """Seconds of collecting/analysing left (run clock minus what SUBMIT needs)."""
        return self.seconds_left() - SUBMIT_RESERVE_S

    def elapsed(self) -> float:
        return time.monotonic() - self.monotonic_start

    def lock(self, name: str) -> asyncio.Lock:
        """A named lock shared by all agents of this run (e.g. so only one agent resolves the site roles)."""
        return self._locks.setdefault(name, asyncio.Lock())

1	"""The blackboard: the one place agents share data. Evidence goes in with its source; results are named values.
2	
3	Everything is JSON-serialisable so a board can be dumped to `.swarm/` and replayed in local development.
4	Single event loop, so no locks; `wait_for` lets a downstream agent start as soon as upstream posts.
5	"""
6	import asyncio
7	import json
8	import time
9	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	
13	@dataclass
14	class Evidence:
15	    kind: str            # label agreed between producer and consumer, e.g. "tender.position" (see docs/SWARM.md)
16	    site: str            # siteId the fact came from
17	    data: dict           # the extracted facts, as found (no interpretation)
18	    source: str = ""     # URL / document / mail subject: where exactly it was read
19	    author: str = ""     # agent name
20	    note: str = ""       # caveats: superseded? withdrawn? timezone? uncertain?
21	    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
22	
23	
24	class Blackboard:
25	    def __init__(self):
26	        self.evidence: list[Evidence] = []
27	        self.results: dict = {}      # named outputs: "quantities", "materials", "prices", "bid", "answer", ...
28	        self.errors: list[dict] = []
29	        self._changed = asyncio.Condition()
30	
31	    async def post(self, item: Evidence) -> None:
32	        async with self._changed:
33	            self.evidence.append(item)
34	            self._changed.notify_all()
35	
36	    def query(self, kind: str | None = None, site: str | None = None, prefix: bool = False) -> list[Evidence]:
37	        def match(e: Evidence) -> bool:
38	            if kind is not None and not (e.kind.startswith(kind) if prefix else e.kind == kind):
39	                return False
40	            return site is None or e.site == site
41	        return [e for e in self.evidence if match(e)]
42	
43	    async def set(self, key: str, value) -> None:
44	        async with self._changed:
45	            self.results[key] = value
46	            self._changed.notify_all()
47	
48	    def get(self, key: str, default=None):
49	        return self.results.get(key, default)
50	
51	    async def wait_for(self, kind: str | None = None, key: str | None = None, timeout: float = 600):
52	        """Block until evidence of `kind` exists (returns the list) or result `key` is set (returns it)."""
53	        def ready():
54	            if key is not None and key in self.results:
55	                return self.results[key]
56	            if kind is not None and self.query(kind):
57	                return self.query(kind)
58	            return None
59	        async with self._changed:
60	            await asyncio.wait_for(self._changed.wait_for(lambda: ready() is not None), timeout)
61	        return ready()
62	
63	    def error(self, agent: str, message: str) -> None:
64	        self.errors.append({"agent": agent, "error": message, "ts": time.time()})
65	
66	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
67	        return {"evidence": [asdict(e) for e in self.evidence], "results": self.results, "errors": self.errors}
68	
69	    def dump(self, path: Path) -> None:
70	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
71	        path.write_text(json.dumps(self.to_json(), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1, default=str), encoding="utf-8")
72	
73	    @classmethod
74	    def load(cls, path: Path) -> "Blackboard":
75	        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
76	        board = cls()
77	        board.evidence = [Evidence(**e) for e in raw.get("evidence", [])]
78	        board.results = raw.get("results", {})
79	        board.errors = raw.get("errors", [])
80	        return board
81

"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import run as contract
from swarm.orchestrator import run_swarm


async def solve(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool) -> dict | None:
    """Runs the swarm (see docs/SWARM.md). Agents live in agents/; the orchestrator runs them phase by phase.

    For an "api" submission the swarm leaves the answer in board.results["answer"]; for a "site" submission the
    submit agent enters it on the website and the result is None.
    """
    return await run_swarm(task, playwright, scored)


async def main() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    try:
        async with async_playwright() as playwright:
            answer = await solve(task, playwright, scored=bool(token))
    except Exception as error:
        logging.getLogger("agent").error("Workflow failed: %s", error)
        return 1
    if answer is None:
        print("Portal submission confirmed; no API answer to post"
              if task["submission"].get("kind") == "site" else "No answer to submit", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

7	code lists the GAPS on that site: concrete facts the bid needs that no saved page holds (a position without a
8	matching material, a material without status / price scales / stock, a commercial key from the Q&A without its mail,
9	a usable-travel requirement without its technical release, no discount approval, ...). The model (with reasoning) turns
10	the gaps into a few focused jobs, one browser agent each, grouping what one agent can do in one go and skipping gaps the
11	saved pages show do not exist. Jobs run at once, in the site's browser (main tab when free, new tabs otherwise). After
12	each job the affected analyses run again on the new pages, which may reveal the next gaps.
13	
14	No gap is worked on twice, every job states exactly what to read (so no two agents collect the same thing), and a page
15	another agent already saved is not opened again (read_page returns the saved text). Follow-ups stop when nothing is
16	missing, nothing new can be tried, or the collect time is used up.

170	async def refresh(ctx, roles: set[str]) -> None:
171	    """Run the analyses that depend on new pages of `roles` again (each failure is only logged)."""
172	    steps = []

174	        steps += [analyze_quantities.refresh]
