from swarm.context import Context


def inputs(**over) -> dict:
    base = {
        "brief": {"tender_reference": "T-1", "scenario_date": "2031-02-01T09:00:00Z"},
        "tender": {"positions": [{"position": "1", "unit": "Stk", "requirement_ref": "Z"}],
                   "clarifications": [{"number": "1", "date": "2031-01-01", "positions": ["1"], "keys": {}}]},
        "quantities": {"1": {"quantity": 10}}, "requirements": {"Z": {}},
        "materials": {"1": {"material": "M1"}},
        "erp": {"materials": {"M1": {"lead_time_stock_weeks": "1", "lead_time_production_weeks": "6",
                                     "surcharge_mass_g": "0"}},
                "conditions": [{"material": "M1", "valid_from": "2031-01-01", "valid_to": "2031-12-31",
                                "price_unit": "1", "scales": [{"min_qty": "1", "price": "100"}]}],
                "stock": {"M1": {"free": "50"}}},
        "discount": {"percent": "0", "source": "no valid approval found"}, "mail": {},
    }
    base.update(over)
    return base


class Dependencies(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_missing_price_unit_names_its_dependency_and_is_a_gap(self):
        data = inputs()
        del data["erp"]["conditions"][0]["price_unit"]
        bid = compute(data)
        self.assertEqual(bid["answer"]["positions"], [])
        self.assertEqual(bid["unresolved"], {"1": ["erp prices M1"]})
        self.assertIn("price unit", bid["dependencies"]["erp prices M1"]["need"])
        # the coordinator's checks saw a valid condition with scales and reported nothing before
        from agents.coordinate import find_gaps
        board = Blackboard()
        board.results.update(data)
        gaps = {g["id"]: g for g in find_gaps(board, {"tender", "spec", "erp", "mail"}, {"tender": ["bidder q&a"]})}
        self.assertIn("price unit", gaps["erp prices M1"]["need"])

    def test_complete_position_has_no_open_dependency(self):
        bid = compute(inputs())
        self.assertEqual(bid["coverage"]["complete"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(bid["unresolved"], {})
        fields = bid["lines"][0]["fields"]
        self.assertEqual(fields["base"], "verified")
        self.assertEqual(fields["packaging"], "absent")          # the Q&A gives the position no packaging key
        self.assertEqual(fields["lead"], "verified: stock")

    def test_missing_delivery_commitment_is_an_estimate_with_its_dependency(self):
        data = inputs()
        data["tender"]["clarifications"][0]["keys"] = {"delivery_key": "D-1"}
        bid = compute(data)
        line = bid["lines"][0]
        self.assertTrue(line["fields"]["lead"].startswith("estimated"))
        self.assertIn("mail delivery_commitments D-1", line["unresolved"])
        data["mail"] = {"delivery_commitments": {"D-1": {"material": "OTHER", "weeks": "2", "max_total_pieces": "99"}}}
        line = compute(data)["lines"][0]                          # a commitment for another material does not apply
        self.assertEqual(line["fields"]["lead"], "verified: stock (commitment is for another material)")
        self.assertEqual(line["unresolved"], [])
        data["mail"]["delivery_commitments"]["D-1"]["material"] = "M1"
        self.assertEqual(compute(data)["answer"]["positions"][0]["lead_time_weeks"], 2)

    def test_bonus_and_packaging_without_their_mails_are_open_not_zero(self):
        data = inputs()
        data["tender"]["clarifications"][0]["keys"] = {"bonus_plan": "B", "packaging_tariff": "P"}
        data["erp"]["materials"]["M1"]["pieces_per_carton"] = "4"
        bid = compute(data)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(bid["unresolved"]["1"]), ["mail packaging_tariffs P", "mail project_bonus B"])
        self.assertNotIn("rebate_total", bid["answer"]["positions"][0])
        self.assertTrue(bid["lines"][0]["fields"]["bonus"].startswith("estimated"))


class ConditionEvidence(unittest.TestCase):
    SCALES = [{"min_qty": "1", "price": "200"}, {"min_qty": "10", "price": "150"}]

    def price(self, conditions, pieces=10):
        data = inputs()
        data["erp"]["conditions"] = conditions
        bid = compute(data)
        return (bid["answer"]["positions"][0]["base_unit_price"] if bid["answer"]["positions"] else None), bid

    def test_fragment_of_another_record_does_not_complete_the_valid_one(self):
        header = {"material": "M1", "record": "C-1", "valid_from": "2031-01-01", "valid_to": "2031-12-31",
                  "price_unit": "1", "scales": []}
        foreign = {"material": "M1", "record": "C-9", "scales": self.SCALES}
        merged = reconcile_conditions([header, foreign])
        self.assertEqual(len(merged), 2)
        price, bid = self.price([header, foreign])
        self.assertIsNone(price)
        self.assertIn("quantity scales of the valid price condition (record C-1)",
                      bid["dependencies"]["erp prices M1"]["need"])

    def test_record_id_picks_the_right_one_of_several_periods(self):
        old = {"material": "M1", "record": "C-1", "valid_from": "2030-01-01", "valid_to": "2030-12-31",
               "price_unit": "1", "scales": []}
        new = {"material": "M1", "record": "C-2", "valid_from": "2031-01-01", "valid_to": "2031-12-31",
               "price_unit": "1", "scales": []}
        scales_of_old = {"material": "M1", "record": "C-1", "scales": self.SCALES}
        price, bid = self.price([old, new, scales_of_old])
        self.assertIsNone(price)                     # the expired record's scales never price the valid one
        scales_of_new = {"material": "M1", "record": "C-2", "scales": [{"min_qty": "1", "price": "120"}]}
        price, _ = self.price([old, new, scales_of_old, scales_of_new])
        self.assertEqual(price, 120.0)

    def test_two_reads_that_disagree_are_a_conflict_not_a_choice(self):
        a = {"material": "M1", "record": "C-1", "valid_from": "2031-01-01", "valid_to": "2031-12-31",
             "price_unit": "1", "scales": self.SCALES}
        b = dict(a, scales=[{"min_qty": "1", "price": "999"}])
        price, bid = self.price([a, b])
        self.assertIsNone(price)
        self.assertIn("conflicting evidence", bid["dependencies"]["erp prices M1"]["need"])

    def test_late_scale_page_of_the_same_record_completes_it(self):
        header = {"material": "M1", "valid_from": "2031-01-01", "valid_to": "2031-12-31", "price_unit": "1",
                  "scales": []}
        cache = {"h": {"kind": "prices", "url": "https://erp.example/cond/77", "conditions": [header]}}
        other = {"material": "M1", "valid_from": "2030-01-01", "valid_to": "2030-06-30", "price_unit": "1",
                 "scales": [{"min_qty": "1", "price": "5"}]}
        cache["o"] = {"kind": "prices", "url": "https://erp.example/cond/12", "conditions": [other]}
        self.assertIsNone(self.price(erp_view(cache)["conditions"])[0])
        cache["s"] = {"kind": "prices", "url": "https://erp.example/cond/77/scales",
                      "conditions": [{"material": "M1", "scales": self.SCALES}]}       # arrives later
        self.assertEqual(self.price(erp_view(cache)["conditions"])[0], 150.0)

    def test_undated_sole_condition_prices_but_stays_open(self):
        price, bid = self.price([{"material": "M1", "price_unit": "1", "scales": self.SCALES}])
        self.assertEqual(price, 150.0)
        self.assertTrue(bid["lines"][0]["fields"]["base"].startswith("estimated"))
        self.assertIn("validity period", bid["dependencies"]["erp prices M1"]["need"])

1	"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.
2	
3	In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
4	is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
5	nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
6	"""
7	import json
8	import os
9	import time
10	from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
11	from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
12	
13	USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
14	LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'
15	
16	
17	def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
18	    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
19	    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
20	    if token:
21	        headers["x-api-key"] = token
22	    data = None
23	    if payload is not None:
24	        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
25	        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
26	    try:
27	        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
28	            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
29	    except HTTPError as error:
30	        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
31	
32	
33	def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
34	    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.
35	
36	    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
37	    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
38	    """
39	    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
40	    if not token:
41	        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
42	            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
43	        try:
44	            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
45	        except ValueError:
46	            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
47	    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
48	    status, body = 0, ""
49	    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
50	        try:
51	            status, body = http(url, token)
52	        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
53	            status, body = 0, str(error)
54	        if status == 200:
55	            return json.loads(body), token
56	        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
57	            break
58	        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
59	    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")
60	
61	
62	def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
63	    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
64	    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
65	    rather than keep searching."""
66	    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
67	    if not expires_at:
68	        return float("inf")
69	    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)
70	
71	
72	def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
73	    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
74	    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
75	    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
76	    submission = run["submission"]
77	    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
78	        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
79	    if not token:
80	        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
81	    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)

input.content:
"""Turn a saved run log (.swarm/runs/<run>-log.md) into a timeline: where the time went, per agent.

Works on logs of any version: it reads the swarm's own lines (phases, browse steps, analyst results, submission) and,
when present, the runtime timeline's `milestone` / `progress` / `TIMELINE` lines (swarm/timeline.py).

    uv run --no-sync python scripts/timeline.py .swarm/runs/run_xxx-log.md [--gap 30]

Reports (run clock = seconds since the COLLECT phase started):
- milestones: brief, site roles, first page per site, first requirements, first ERP candidates, materials matched,
  each phase, submission attempts, accepted submission (plus the runtime's own milestones)
- per agent: steps, first/last step, busy time, idle gaps longer than --gap seconds (waiting or stalled)
- trouble: state timeouts, empty model replies, crashed browses, cleanup overruns, model timeouts, failed extractions
The log holds scenario values: read the output, never copy values from it into the package.
"""
import argparse
import re
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

LINE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}),(\d{3}) (\S+) (.*)$")
STEP = re.compile(r"^(\S+) step (\d+): (.*)$")
TROUBLE = {"state timeouts": "repeated browser-state timeouts", "no model reply": "step \\d+: no reply",
           "crashed browses": "browser agent failed|swarm \\w+ failed", "cleanup overruns": "cleanup exceeded",
           "model timeouts": "LLM call timed out|model TimeoutError", "failed extractions": "extract chunk failed",
           "hung tabs closed": "closed a hung tab", "browser moved": "is unreachable"}
MILESTONES = [("brief read", r"BriefReader brief facts"), ("site roles", r"sites site roles"),
              ("first requirements", r"RequirementAnalyzer current revision \S+, requirements \[['\"]"),
              ("positions known", r"QuantityAnalyzer [1-9]\d* positions"),
              ("first ERP candidates", r"search \S+: candidates \[['\"]"),
              ("first draft bid", r"BidDrafter draft: [1-9]"), ("materials matched", r"MaterialMatcher materials:"),
              ("collect end", r"phase VERIFY"), ("submit start", r"phase SUBMIT"),
              ("submission attempt", r"submission attempt \d+ finished"),
              ("accepted", r"portal acceptance confirmed|milestone accepted submission")]


def parse(path: Path):
    events = []
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        m = LINE.match(raw.strip())
        if m:
            ts = datetime.strptime(m.group(1), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S").timestamp() + int(m.group(2)) / 1000
            events.append((ts, m.group(3), m.group(4)))
    events.sort(key=lambda e: e[0])
    return events


def clock(s: float) -> str:
    s = max(0, int(s))
    return f"{s // 60:02d}:{s % 60:02d}"


def analyse(events, gap: float) -> str:
    if not events:

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Start a sandbox test run of this package (public data, unscored) and optionally follow its key log lines.

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1                 # unit tests, then start the run; prints its id and page
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -Follow         # ... and stream milestones + failures until the run ends
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -SkipTests -Follow

  From Git Bash / a Claude Code Monitor:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/test-run.ps1 -Follow
#>
param(
    [switch]$Follow,       # stream milestone/failure lines of the run's log until it ends
    [switch]$SkipTests,    # skip the local unit tests before packing
    [switch]$Open,         # open the run page in the browser
    [switch]$DryRun        # only show what would be packed
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)

# Lines worth seeing while a run goes: phases, scraper/analyst results, the submission, and every kind of failure.
$Milestones = 'browse done|swarm phase|site roles|brief facts|early requirements|current revision|positions,|' +
              'discount \{|materials:|verification:|submission attempt|answer \(entered|model calls:|nothing saved|' +
              'board after collect|gaps|follow-up|candidates|tip for|guard .*->|' +
              'tab job failed|timed out|failed|Traceback|FATAL|CRITICAL|No lifecycle events'

if (-not $SkipTests) {
    Write-Host "== unit tests"
    $tests = cmd /c "uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q 2>&1"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $tests | Select-Object -Last 40; throw "unit tests failed: not starting a test run" }
    $tests | Select-String -Pattern '^Ran \d+ tests|^OK' | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
}

if ($DryRun) {
    atira test-run . --dry-run
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

Write-Host "== starting test run"
$openFlag = if ($Open) { "" } else { "--no-open" }
# atira prints the run id on stderr: merge it in cmd (PowerShell 5.1 would turn stderr lines into errors).
$out = (cmd /c "atira test-run . $openFlag 2>&1" | Out-String)
Write-Host $out.Trim()
$runId = [regex]::Match($out, 'run_[0-9a-f]{16}').Value
if (-not $runId) { throw "no run id in the atira output" }

Write-Host "== run $runId  https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/$runId"
if (-not $Follow) {
    Write-Host "follow its log: atira logs $runId --follow"
    exit 0
}

# The whole log goes to .swarm/runs/<run>-log.md (git-ignored, never packaged; see CLAUDE.md "Run data"), the milestones
# to the console. cmd merges stderr into stdout without PowerShell 5.1 wrapping each stderr line as an error record.
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force ".swarm/runs" | Out-Null
$logFile = ".swarm/runs/$runId-log.md"
Set-Content -Encoding utf8 $logFile ("# $runId log`n`nFollowed from the start by scripts/test-run.ps1.`n`n" + '```text')
cmd /c "atira logs $runId --follow 2>&1" | ForEach-Object {
    Add-Content -Encoding utf8 $logFile $_
    if ($_ -match $Milestones) { $_ }
}

Write-Host "== log stream of $runId ended; whole log in $logFile"

input.old_string:
## Time budget (20-minute run)

`SUBMIT_RESERVE_S` (default 600 s, env `SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S`): collecting/analysing stops that long before expiry,
then VERIFY/COMPUTE (instant) and SUBMIT, which stops `FINAL_MARGIN_S` (40 s) before expiry.
input.new_string:
## Time budget (20-minute run)

Collecting/analysing stops `ctx.submit_reserve()` seconds before expiry, then VERIFY/COMPUTE (instant) and SUBMIT,
which stops `FINAL_MARGIN_S` (40 s) before expiry. The reserve is estimated live: (wizard steps + 2.5 steps per
position, minus the steps WizardPrep already did) x measured median browsing step x 1.5 (full reasoning) + TAN lookup +
safety, clamped to [390, 600] s. `SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S` > 0 fixes it. The collect cutoff and every browse's stop mark
follow the live value (re-checked each second / before each step).

## Where the time goes (swarm/timeline.py, scripts/timeline.py)

Spans per agent: `browse.step`, `model.queue` (waiting for a slot), `model.call`, `extract`, `wait.dep` (an agent
waiting for an upstream result), `recovery` (browser checks, hung tabs, failed model attempts), `guard`, `browse.failed`;
counters for repeated work (`reads.repeat`, `browse.retries`, `erp.focused`, `browse.crashed`, ...); milestones (first
page per site, first requirements, first usable bid, each position complete, wizard ready, collect end, submit start,
TAN requested/received, entries checked, accepted submission). The run log gets a `progress` line per minute and five
`TIMELINE` lines at the end (the platform keeps only the log's tail); local runs also write `.swarm/timeline.json`.
`scripts/timeline.py <saved log>` rebuilds a timeline from any run log, old or new.

## Coordination (what no longer waits)

- `BidDrafter` recomputes the bid every 3 s during collection (`results["bid_draft"]`); the submitter falls back to it.
- `compute()` names an open dependency for every omitted position and estimated field (`dependencies`, `unresolved`,
  per-line `fields` status: verified / absent / estimated / missing). The coordinator turns those into gaps too, so a
  condition without a price unit is a gap, not "no gaps". Mail gaps start 30 s after the index pass was analysed; a site
  with follow-ups running takes new, different gaps (max 2 at once per site); an unchanged gap set is re-planned only
  after 45 s.
- ERP: the next job is chosen when a tab is free: focused re-reads of what the calculation misses, then prices/stock of
  materials that already match a position, then searches and the best candidate per requirement, then other
  candidates; candidates of already matched positions last. Extraction runs in the background (the tab moves on).
- Analysts extract each page in its own task (`swarm.extract.start_once`): a new page never waits for a slow batch.
- Price conditions: `reconcile_conditions` merges pages of one record only (same record id, linked page URLs, or a
  single dated condition); conflicting reads become `_conflict` (unpriced, a gap), unrelated fragments stay apart.

## Recovery

- A hung-tab check closes only the caller's tab, unowned tabs and idle owned tabs, never another agent's active tab;
  a healthy browser is not re-checked within 20 s. A hung own tab is renewed in place (main tabs stay main tabs).
- A crashed browse returns an unfinished result (its pages are already saved); `browse_until_done` retries with the
  saved topics instead of losing the scraper.
- Browsing model calls time out after 35 s (`SWARM_BROWSE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_S`) instead of 55 s.

## Submission

`WizardPrep` opens the bid wizard in browser 0's main tab near the end of collection (entering nothing); at submit
start the mail main tab logs in and opens the inbox; `check_entries` compares the summary page with the bid in code.

+waiting for an upstream result), `recovery` (browser checks, hung tabs, failed model attempts), `guard`, `browse.failed`;
+page per site, first requirements, first usable bid, each position complete, wizard ready, collect end, submit start,
+TAN requested/received, entries checked, accepted submission). The run log gets a `progress` line per minute and five
+`TIMELINE` lines at the end (the platform keeps only the log's tail); local runs also write `.swarm/timeline.json`.
+`scripts/timeline.py <saved log>` rebuilds a timeline from any run log, old or new.
+- `BidDrafter` recomputes the bid every 3 s during collection (`results["bid_draft"]`); the submitter falls back to it.
+- `compute()` names an open dependency for every omitted position and estimated field (`dependencies`, `unresolved`,
+  per-line `fields` status: verified / absent / estimated / missing). The coordinator turns those into gaps too, so a
+  condition without a price unit is a gap, not "no gaps". Mail gaps start 30 s after the index pass was analysed; a site
+  with follow-ups running takes new, different gaps (max 2 at once per site); an unchanged gap set is re-planned only
+- ERP: the next job is chosen when a tab is free: focused re-reads of what the calculation misses, then prices/stock of
+  materials that already match a position, then searches and the best candidate per requirement, then other
+  candidates; candidates of already matched positions last. Extraction runs in the background (the tab moves on).
+- Analysts extract each page in its own task (`swarm.extract.start_once`): a new page never waits for a slow batch.
+- Price conditions: `reconcile_conditions` merges pages of one record only (same record id, linked page URLs, or a
+  single dated condition); conflicting reads become `_conflict` (unpriced, a gap), unrelated fragments stay apart.
+- A hung-tab check closes only the caller's tab, unowned tabs and idle owned tabs, never another agent's active tab;
+  a healthy browser is not re-checked within 20 s. A hung own tab is renewed in place (main tabs stay main tabs).
+- A crashed browse returns an unfinished result (its pages are already saved); `browse_until_done` retries with the
+  saved topics instead of losing the scraper.
+- Browsing model calls time out after 35 s (`SWARM_BROWSE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_S`) instead of 55 s.
+`WizardPrep` opens the bid wizard in browser 0's main tab near the end of collection (entering nothing); at submit
+start the mail main tab logs in and opens the inbox; `check_entries` compares the summary page with the bid in code.
`RUN_LIMIT_S` (default 1200 s, env `SWARM_RUN_LIMIT_S`, 0 = off): every run plans with at most 20 minutes from process
start, so 2-hour test runs show the timing of a scored run.

The baseline (`main`) is the one project everyone builds on. This file says what came from which branch, what was
superseded by what, and which questions are still open. Update it when you integrate something (`scripts/team.py`).

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S > 0 fixes the reserve; by default it is estimated during the run from the positions to enter

SUBMIT_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 0)) or 600     # the upper bound / fixed value
FIXED_RESERVE = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 0)) > 0
MIN_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_MIN_RESERVE_S", 390))
MAX_RESERVE_S = SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
FINAL_MARGIN_S = 40
# Submission model, in browsing steps: wizard steps independent of the positions (login, tender, wizard start, bidder,
# decision, documents, TAN request/entry, summary, confirmation, receipt), steps per position, and the steps the
# wizard warm-up (agents/submit_bid.WizardPrep) already did. Full-reasoning submitter steps are slower than the
# flash steps measured during collection. TAN lookup runs next to the wizard and costs extra time only at the end.
BASE_STEPS, STEPS_PER_POSITION, PREP_SAVES_STEPS = 12, 2.5, 4
FULL_REASONING_FACTOR, TAN_S, SAFETY_S = 1.5, 60, 45

# start, so test runs show the timing (and the follow-ups that fit) of a scored run. The run's real expiry still wins

RUN_LIMIT_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_RUN_LIMIT_S", 1200))

class Context:

    board: Blackboard
    llm: LLM
    pool: object                      # swarm.browser_pool.BrowserPool (None in unit tests)
    scored: bool = False              # True in a real run (has a run token); False for local scouting
    t0: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    monotonic_start: float = field(default_factory=time.monotonic)
    _locks: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)
    shared: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)   # in-memory objects agents share (queues); never dumped

    @property
    def brief(self) -> str:
        return self.task["brief"]

    def site(self, site_id: str) -> dict:
        """The access entry (siteId, url, credentials) of a website, e.g. ctx.site("erp")."""
        for entry in self.task["access"]:
            if entry.get("siteId") == site_id:
                return entry
        raise KeyError(f"no site {site_id!r}; have {[s.get('siteId') for s in self.task['access']]}")

    @property
    def site_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        return [s.get("siteId") for s in self.task["access"]]

    def seconds_left(self) -> float:
        left = contract.seconds_left(self.task)
        simulated = os.environ.get("SWARM_DEADLINE_S")          # local runs: pretend the run lasts this long
        if left == float("inf") and simulated and not self.scored:
            return float(simulated) - self.elapsed()
        return min(left, RUN_LIMIT_S - self.elapsed()) if RUN_LIMIT_S > 0 else left

    def time_left(self) -> float:
        """Seconds of collecting/analysing left (run clock minus what SUBMIT needs)."""
        return self.seconds_left() - self.submit_reserve()

        """What SUBMIT needs, from the positions to enter and the measured step pace (fixed when configured)."""
        if FIXED_RESERVE:
            return SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
        from swarm import timeline
        positions = len((self.board.get("tender") or {}).get("positions") or []) or 5
        step = min(30.0, max(6.0, timeline.current().median_step()))
        steps = BASE_STEPS - (PREP_SAVES_STEPS if self.shared.get("wizard_ready") else 0) + STEPS_PER_POSITION * positions
        estimate = steps * step * FULL_REASONING_FACTOR + TAN_S + SAFETY_S + FINAL_MARGIN_S
        return min(MAX_RESERVE_S, max(MIN_RESERVE_S, estimate))

    def stop_at(self, extra: float = 0.0) -> float:
        """Seconds-left mark at which collection work with `extra` seconds of follow-up analysis must stop."""
        return self.submit_reserve() + extra

    def elapsed(self) -> float:
        return time.monotonic() - self.monotonic_start

    def lock(self, name: str) -> asyncio.Lock:
        """A named lock shared by all agents of this run (e.g. so only one agent resolves the site roles)."""
        return self._locks.setdefault(name, asyncio.Lock())

class RunClosedBySubmission(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_finished_token_after_signing_counts_as_accepted_and_stops_retries(self):
        from agents import submit_bid
        from swarm import timeline
        timeline.reset()
        ctx = Context(task={"brief": "Submit.", "submission": {"kind": "site"}, "access": [
            {"siteId": "t", "url": "https://t.example"}, {"siteId": "m", "url": "https://m.example"}]},
            board=Blackboard(), llm=None, pool=None)
        ctx.board.results.update({"sites": {"tender": "t", "spec": "t", "erp": "t", "mail": "m"},
                                  "brief": {"tender_reference": "FIXTURE"}})
        attempts = []

        async def fake_browse(ctx_, goal, **kwargs):
            if kwargs["author"].endswith(".mailbox"):
                return {"summary": "", "done": True, "steps": 1}
            attempts.append(1)
            timeline.mark("TAN requested")
            ba.note_run_closed(ctx, RuntimeError("Error code: 401 - unknown, finished or expired run token"))
            return {"summary": "", "done": False, "steps": 4}
        with mock.patch.object(submit_bid, "browse", fake_browse):
            await submit_bid.BidSubmitter(ctx).run()
        self.assertEqual(len(attempts), 1)
        self.assertTrue(ctx.board.get("submission")["accepted"])
        self.assertIn("accepted submission", timeline.current().milestones)


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""Recovery that preserves work: a hung-tab check never closes another agent's active tab (real Chromium), a hung
tab of the caller is renewed in place, and a browse that crashes resumes with what is already saved."""
import asyncio
import http.server
import json
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.request
from unittest import mock

from swarm import browser_agent as ba
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard, Evidence
from swarm.context import Context
from tests.test_hung_tabs import Handler, free_port


class HungTabsOfOthers(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_only_own_unowned_and_idle_tabs_are_closed(self):
        from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

        server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        base, port = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}", free_port()

        async def run():
            async with async_playwright() as p:
                browser = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True, args=[f"--remote-debugging-port={port}"])
                context = await browser.new_context()
                pages = [await context.new_page() for _ in range(3)]
                for page in pages:
                    await page.goto(base + "/")
                listed = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/list", timeout=5))
                ids = {t["url"] + str(i): t["id"] for i, t in enumerate(t for t in listed if t["type"] == "page")}
                targets = [t["id"] for t in listed if t["type"] == "page" and t["url"].startswith(base)]
                for page in pages:                     # every page hangs (a request that never answers)
                    await page.evaluate(f"setTimeout(() => location.href = '{base}/?block', 10)")
                await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
                other, mine, idle = ba.Tab(0), ba.Tab(0), ba.Tab(0)
                other.claim(targets[0])
                mine.claim(targets[1])
                idle.claim(targets[2])
                ba._ACTIVE.update({other, mine})       # `other` is another agent's tab with a browse running
                try:
                    with mock.patch.object(ba.browsers, "cdp_urls", return_value=[f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"]), \
                            mock.patch.object(ba, "TAB_PROBE_S", 3):
                        closed = await ba.close_hung_tabs(0, mine=mine)
                finally:
                    ba._ACTIVE.difference_update({other, mine})
                    for t in (other, mine, idle):

        tab.suspect = True

            return True

        async def hung(browser, keep=None, mine=None):
            return ["dead-target"]
        with mock.patch.object(ba.browsers, "cdp_urls", return_value=["http://127.0.0.1:1"]), \
                mock.patch.object(ba, "browser_responds", responds), mock.patch.object(ba, "close_hung_tabs", hung):
            again = asyncio.run(ba.responsive_tab(tab))
        self.assertIs(again, tab)
        self.assertIs(ba.main_tab(3), tab)
        self.assertTrue(tab.renewed and tab.target_id is None and not tab.used)
        self.assertNotIn("dead-target", ba._OWNERS)
        ba._MAIN_TABS.pop(3, None)

- live reserve: submitter steps never assumed faster than 18 s (collection steps are much faster)

"""Everything an agent gets: the task, the blackboard, the model, the browsers and the clock."""
import asyncio
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import run as contract
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.llm import LLM

# Collecting and analysing stop `submit_reserve()` seconds before expiry; the rest belongs to SUBMIT (filling the bid
# form and signing takes several minutes of browser steps). SUBMIT itself stops FINAL_MARGIN_S before expiry.
# signing 4 positions took 466 s in run_7732ba545b50b3a5 and ended 60 s before expiry; a 5th position adds ~90 s.
# SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S > 0 fixes the reserve; by default it is estimated during the run from the positions to enter
# and the measured pace of browsing steps (see Context.submit_reserve), within [MIN_RESERVE_S, MAX_RESERVE_S].
SUBMIT_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 0)) or 600     # the upper bound / fixed value
FIXED_RESERVE = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 0)) > 0
MIN_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_MIN_RESERVE_S", 390))
MAX_RESERVE_S = SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
FINAL_MARGIN_S = 40
# Submission model, in browsing steps: wizard steps independent of the positions (login, tender, wizard start, bidder,
# decision, documents, TAN request/entry, summary, confirmation, receipt), steps per position, and the steps the
# wizard warm-up (agents/submit_bid.WizardPrep) already did. Full-reasoning submitter steps are slower than the
# flash steps measured during collection. TAN lookup runs next to the wizard and costs extra time only at the end.
BASE_STEPS, STEPS_PER_POSITION, PREP_SAVES_STEPS = 12, 2.5, 4
FULL_REASONING_FACTOR, TAN_S, SAFETY_S = 1.5, 60, 45
# Collection steps (logins, clicks) are much faster than the submitter's full-reasoning steps: run_7732ba545b50b3a5
# signed 4 positions in 466 s, ~21 s per estimated step. A submitter step is never assumed faster than this.
MIN_SUBMIT_STEP_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_MIN_SUBMIT_STEP_S", 18))
# A scored run lasts 20 minutes; test runs may last 2 hours. Every run plans with at most RUN_LIMIT_S from process
# start, so test runs show the timing (and the follow-ups that fit) of a scored run. The run's real expiry still wins
# when it is earlier.
RUN_LIMIT_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_RUN_LIMIT_S", 1200))


@dataclass
class Context:
    task: dict
    board: Blackboard
    llm: LLM
    pool: object                      # swarm.browser_pool.BrowserPool (None in unit tests)
    scored: bool = False              # True in a real run (has a run token); False for local scouting
    t0: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    monotonic_start: float = field(default_factory=time.monotonic)
    _locks: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)
    shared: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)   # in-memory objects agents share (queues); never dumped

    @property
    def brief(self) -> str:
        return self.task["brief"]

    def site(self, site_id: str) -> dict:
        """The access entry (siteId, url, credentials) of a website, e.g. ctx.site("erp")."""
        for entry in self.task["access"]:
            if entry.get("siteId") == site_id:
                return entry
        raise KeyError(f"no site {site_id!r}; have {[s.get('siteId') for s in self.task['access']]}")

    @property
    def site_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        return [s.get("siteId") for s in self.task["access"]]

    def seconds_left(self) -> float:
        left = contract.seconds_left(self.task)
        simulated = os.environ.get("SWARM_DEADLINE_S")          # local runs: pretend the run lasts this long
        if left == float("inf") and simulated and not self.scored:
            return float(simulated) - self.elapsed()
        return min(left, RUN_LIMIT_S - self.elapsed()) if RUN_LIMIT_S > 0 else left

    def time_left(self) -> float:
        """Seconds of collecting/analysing left (run clock minus what SUBMIT needs)."""
        return self.seconds_left() - self.submit_reserve()

    def submit_reserve(self) -> float:
        """What SUBMIT needs, from the positions to enter and the measured step pace (fixed when configured)."""
        if FIXED_RESERVE:
            return SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
        from swarm import timeline
        positions = len((self.board.get("tender") or {}).get("positions") or []) or 5
        step = min(30.0, max(6.0, timeline.current().median_step()))
        steps = BASE_STEPS - (PREP_SAVES_STEPS if self.shared.get("wizard_ready") else 0) + STEPS_PER_POSITION * positions
        submit_step = max(MIN_SUBMIT_STEP_S, step * FULL_REASONING_FACTOR)
        estimate = steps * submit_step + TAN_S + SAFETY_S + FINAL_MARGIN_S
        return min(MAX_RESERVE_S, max(MIN_RESERVE_S, estimate))

    def stop_at(self, extra: float = 0.0) -> float:
        """Seconds-left mark at which collection work with `extra` seconds of follow-up analysis must stop."""
        return self.submit_reserve() + extra

    def elapsed(self) -> float:
        return time.monotonic() - self.monotonic_start

    def lock(self, name: str) -> asyncio.Lock:
        """A named lock shared by all agents of this run (e.g. so only one agent resolves the site roles)."""
        return self._locks.setdefault(name, asyncio.Lock())

"""Base class for site scrapers: a model-driven browse of ONE site that streams Evidence onto the blackboard.

Subclass, set `role` ('tender' | 'spec' | 'erp' | 'mail') and `browser`, and write `goal()` (what the model should
find, in general terms derived from the brief; never scenario values). The site id for the role is resolved at run
time (datasets name their sites differently). Override `run()` for several browse passes; call `self.browse(goal)`.

When the scraper ends (done, failed or out of time) it sets results[f"done.{role}"] so analysts waiting on it start.
Independent jobs run at once with `browse_in_tabs` (one new tab each, closed when its job ends); `self.browse` works
in the browser's main tab.
"""
import asyncio

from swarm import timeline
from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import Tab, browse
from swarm.extract import brief_intro
from swarm.sites import site_for

ANALYSIS_RESERVE_S = 75     # scrapers stop browsing this long before collecting ends (analysts need the time)


class SiteScraper(Agent):
    phase = Phase.COLLECT
    role: str = ""
    site_id: str = ""
    max_steps: int = 40
    hints: str = ""

    def goal(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def login_text(self) -> str:
        site = self.ctx.site(self.site_id)
        creds = site.get("credentials") or {}
        return f"Site ({self.role}): {site['url']}\nLogin: username {creds.get('username')!r}, password {creds.get('password')!r}"

    def task_text(self) -> str:

"""Everything an agent gets: the task, the blackboard, the model, the browsers and the clock."""
import asyncio
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import run as contract
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.llm import LLM

# Collecting and analysing stop `submit_reserve()` seconds before expiry; the rest belongs to SUBMIT (filling the bid
# form and signing takes several minutes of browser steps). SUBMIT itself stops FINAL_MARGIN_S before expiry.
# signing 4 positions took 466 s in run_7732ba545b50b3a5 and ended 60 s before expiry; a 5th position adds ~90 s.
# SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S > 0 fixes the reserve; by default it is estimated during the run from the positions to enter
# and the measured pace of browsing steps (see Context.submit_reserve), within [MIN_RESERVE_S, MAX_RESERVE_S].
SUBMIT_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 0)) or 600     # the upper bound / fixed value
FIXED_RESERVE = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 0)) > 0
MIN_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_MIN_RESERVE_S", 390))
MAX_RESERVE_S = SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
FINAL_MARGIN_S = 40
# Submission model, in browsing steps: wizard steps independent of the positions (login, tender, wizard start, bidder,
# decision, documents, TAN request/entry, summary, confirmation, receipt), steps per position, and the steps the
# wizard warm-up (agents/submit_bid.WizardPrep) already did. Full-reasoning submitter steps are slower than the
# flash steps measured during collection. TAN lookup runs next to the wizard and costs extra time only at the end.
# run_7b060fa870cea9b6: an entered position took 3 steps (one 6: cascading selects), an omitted one 1 step
BASE_STEPS, STEPS_PER_POSITION, PREP_SAVES_STEPS = 12, 3, 4
FULL_REASONING_FACTOR, TAN_S, SAFETY_S = 1.5, 60, 45
# Collection steps (logins, clicks) are much faster than the submitter's full-reasoning steps: run_7732ba545b50b3a5
# signed 4 positions in 466 s, ~21 s per estimated step. A submitter step is never assumed faster than this.
MIN_SUBMIT_STEP_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_MIN_SUBMIT_STEP_S", 18))
# A scored run lasts 20 minutes; test runs may last 2 hours. Every run plans with at most RUN_LIMIT_S from process
# start, so test runs show the timing (and the follow-ups that fit) of a scored run. The run's real expiry still wins
# when it is earlier.
RUN_LIMIT_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_RUN_LIMIT_S", 1200))


@dataclass
class Context:
    task: dict
    board: Blackboard
    llm: LLM
    pool: object                      # swarm.browser_pool.BrowserPool (None in unit tests)
    scored: bool = False              # True in a real run (has a run token); False for local scouting
    t0: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    monotonic_start: float = field(default_factory=time.monotonic)
    _locks: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)
    shared: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)   # in-memory objects agents share (queues); never dumped

    @property
    def brief(self) -> str:
        return self.task["brief"]

    def site(self, site_id: str) -> dict:
        """The access entry (siteId, url, credentials) of a website, e.g. ctx.site("erp")."""
        for entry in self.task["access"]:
            if entry.get("siteId") == site_id:
                return entry
        raise KeyError(f"no site {site_id!r}; have {[s.get('siteId') for s in self.task['access']]}")

    @property
    def site_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        return [s.get("siteId") for s in self.task["access"]]

    def seconds_left(self) -> float:
        left = contract.seconds_left(self.task)
        simulated = os.environ.get("SWARM_DEADLINE_S")          # local runs: pretend the run lasts this long
        if left == float("inf") and simulated and not self.scored:
            return float(simulated) - self.elapsed()
        return min(left, RUN_LIMIT_S - self.elapsed()) if RUN_LIMIT_S > 0 else left

    def time_left(self) -> float:
        """Seconds of collecting/analysing left (run clock minus what SUBMIT needs)."""
        return self.seconds_left() - self.submit_reserve()

    def submit_reserve(self) -> float:
        """What SUBMIT needs, from the positions to enter and the measured step pace (fixed when configured)."""
        if FIXED_RESERVE:
            return SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
        from swarm import timeline
        positions = len((self.board.get("tender") or {}).get("positions") or []) or 5
        step = min(30.0, max(6.0, timeline.current().median_step()))
        steps = BASE_STEPS - (PREP_SAVES_STEPS if self.shared.get("wizard_ready") else 0) + STEPS_PER_POSITION * positions
        submit_step = max(MIN_SUBMIT_STEP_S, step * FULL_REASONING_FACTOR)
        estimate = steps * submit_step + TAN_S + SAFETY_S + FINAL_MARGIN_S
        return min(MAX_RESERVE_S, max(MIN_RESERVE_S, estimate))

    def stop_at(self, extra: float = 0.0) -> float:
        """Seconds-left mark at which collection work with `extra` seconds of follow-up analysis must stop."""
        return self.submit_reserve() + extra

    def elapsed(self) -> float:
        return time.monotonic() - self.monotonic_start

    def lock(self, name: str) -> asyncio.Lock:
        """A named lock shared by all agents of this run (e.g. so only one agent resolves the site roles)."""
        return self._locks.setdefault(name, asyncio.Lock())

"""Recovery that preserves work: a hung-tab check never closes another agent's active tab (real Chromium), a hung
tab of the caller is renewed in place, and a browse that crashes resumes with what is already saved."""
import asyncio
import http.server
import json
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.request
from unittest import mock

from swarm import browser_agent as ba
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard, Evidence
from swarm.context import Context
from tests.test_hung_tabs import Handler, free_port


class HungTabsOfOthers(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_only_own_unowned_and_idle_tabs_are_closed(self):
        from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

        server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        base, port = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}", free_port()

        async def run():
            async with async_playwright() as p:
                browser = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True, args=[f"--remote-debugging-port={port}"])
                context = await browser.new_context()
                pages = [await context.new_page() for _ in range(3)]
                for page in pages:
                    await page.goto(base + "/")
                listed = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/list", timeout=5))
                ids = {t["url"] + str(i): t["id"] for i, t in enumerate(t for t in listed if t["type"] == "page")}
                targets = [t["id"] for t in listed if t["type"] == "page" and t["url"].startswith(base)]
                for page in pages:                     # every page hangs (a request that never answers)
                    await page.evaluate(f"setTimeout(() => location.href = '{base}/?block', 10)")
                await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
                other, mine, idle = ba.Tab(0), ba.Tab(0), ba.Tab(0)
                other.claim(targets[0])
                mine.claim(targets[1])
                idle.claim(targets[2])
                ba._ACTIVE.update({other, mine})       # `other` is another agent's tab with a browse running
                try:
                    with mock.patch.object(ba.browsers, "cdp_urls", return_value=[f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"]), \
                            mock.patch.object(ba, "TAB_PROBE_S", 3):
                        closed = await ba.close_hung_tabs(0, mine=mine)
                finally:
                    ba._ACTIVE.difference_update({other, mine})
                    for t in (other, mine, idle):
                        ba._OWNERS.pop(t.target_id, None)
                await browser.close()
                return closed, targets, ids

        closed, targets, _ = asyncio.run(run())
        server.shutdown()
        self.assertNotIn(targets[0], closed)          # another agent's active tab: never touched
        self.assertIn(targets[1], closed)             # the caller's own hung tab
        self.assertIn(targets[2], closed)             # an owned tab nobody is browsing in


class RenewInPlace(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_hung_own_tab_is_renewed_and_main_tab_stays_main(self):
        tab = ba.main_tab(3)
        tab.claim("dead-target")
        tab.suspect = True

        async def responds(browser, timeout=12):
            return True

        async def hung(browser, keep=None, mine=None):
            return ["dead-target"]
        with mock.patch.object(ba.browsers, "cdp_urls", return_value=["http://127.0.0.1:1"]), \
                mock.patch.object(ba, "browser_responds", responds), mock.patch.object(ba, "close_hung_tabs", hung):
            again = asyncio.run(ba.responsive_tab(tab))
        self.assertIs(again, tab)
        self.assertIs(ba.main_tab(3), tab)
        self.assertTrue(tab.renewed and tab.target_id is None and not tab.used)
        self.assertNotIn("dead-target", ba._OWNERS)
        ba._MAIN_TABS.pop(3, None)

    def test_healthy_recently_checked_browser_is_not_probed_again(self):
        calls = []

        async def responds(browser, timeout=12):
            calls.append(browser)
            return True

        async def none(browser, keep=None, mine=None):
            return []
        with mock.patch.object(ba.browsers, "cdp_urls", return_value=["http://127.0.0.1:1"]), \
                mock.patch.object(ba, "browser_responds", responds), mock.patch.object(ba, "close_hung_tabs", none):
            ba._CHECKED.pop(0, None)
            asyncio.run(ba.responsive_tab(ba.Tab(0)))
            asyncio.run(ba.responsive_tab(ba.Tab(0)))
            suspect = ba.Tab(0)
            suspect.suspect = True
            asyncio.run(ba.responsive_tab(suspect))
        self.assertEqual(calls, [0, 0])               # second healthy check skipped; a suspect tab is checked
        ba._CHECKED.pop(0, None)


class CrashResume(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_crashed_browse_is_retried_with_what_is_saved(self):
        from swarm import scraper as sc

        class Fixture(sc.SiteScraper):
            role, browser, site_id = "spec", 1, "s"

            def goal(self):
                return "collect"
        ctx = Context(task={"brief": "", "access": [{"siteId": "s", "url": "https://s.example", "credentials": {}}]},
                      board=Blackboard(), llm=None, pool=None)
        jobs = []

        async def fake_browse(ctx_, prompt, **kwargs):
            jobs.append(prompt)
            if len(jobs) == 1:
                await kwargs["on_record"]({"kind": "page", "data": {"topic": "spec revisions", "text": "x"},
                                           "source": "u", "note": ""})
                raise RuntimeError("CDP connection lost")
            return {"summary": "requirements saved", "done": True, "records": [], "steps": 3}
        with mock.patch.object(sc, "browse", fake_browse):
            out = await Fixture(ctx).browse_until_done("read the requirement table", attempts=3)
        self.assertTrue(out["done"])
        self.assertEqual(len(jobs), 2)
        self.assertIn("Already saved: ['spec revisions']", jobs[1])      # resumes; does not start over
        self.assertEqual(len(ctx.board.query("spec.page")), 1)            # the first attempt's page survived


class RunClosedBySubmission(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_finished_token_after_signing_counts_as_accepted_and_stops_retries(self):
        from agents import submit_bid
        from swarm import timeline
        timeline.reset()
        ctx = Context(task={"brief": "Submit.", "submission": {"kind": "site"}, "access": [
            {"siteId": "t", "url": "https://t.example"}, {"siteId": "m", "url": "https://m.example"}]},
            board=Blackboard(), llm=None, pool=None)
        ctx.board.results.update({"sites": {"tender": "t", "spec": "t", "erp": "t", "mail": "m"},
                                  "brief": {"tender_reference": "FIXTURE"}})
        attempts = []

        async def fake_browse(ctx_, goal, **kwargs):
            if kwargs["author"].endswith(".mailbox"):
                return {"summary": "", "done": True, "steps": 1}
            attempts.append(1)
            timeline.mark("TAN requested")
            ba.note_run_closed(ctx, RuntimeError("Error code: 401 - unknown, finished or expired run token"))
            return {"summary": "", "done": False, "steps": 4}
        with mock.patch.object(submit_bid, "browse", fake_browse):
            await submit_bid.BidSubmitter(ctx).run()
        self.assertEqual(len(attempts), 1)
        self.assertTrue(ctx.board.get("submission")["accepted"])
        self.assertIn("accepted submission", timeline.current().milestones)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
